question: Under the US Advanced Battery Consortium standard, when does an EV battery reach the end of its usable life, what can be done with such batteries, and which of those does the review say they all eventually need?
rendered:
According to the text on page 2 of "Energy and environmental aspects in recycling lithium-ion batteries: Concept of Battery Identity Global Passport", under the US Advanced Battery Consortium standard, an EV battery reaches the end of its usable life when its current cell capacity is less than 80% of the rated capacity. 

At this point, those end-of-life EV batteries can be reused/repurposed, recycled, or disposed in landfills. However, the review states that all of these eventualities are necessary, as eventually, all batteries will need to be recycled.
